edges.mechanism: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion; additive with vitamin D-driven calcium absorption, risk of hypercalcemia (labelled for ergocalciferol in hypoparathyroidism and for calcitriol).
edges.evidence: FDA labels (calcitriol, ergocalciferol) plus narrative review of drug-related hypercalcemia; no RCT with OTC D3.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin D-induced hypercalcemia may precipitate cardiac arrhythmias in patients on digitalis.
edges.evidence: FDA calcitriol label precaution; extrapolated to native vitamin D (only relevant if hypercalcemia occurs).

edges.mechanism: Fat malabsorption reduces absorption of fat-soluble vitamins including vitamin D.
edges.evidence: Small clinical study in adolescents: 25(OH)D fell after 1 month of orlistat despite a multivitamin.

edges.mechanism: Cholestyramine binds fat-soluble vitamins in the gut, reducing absorption.
edges.evidence: FDA calcitriol label statement; no modern RCT data.

edges.mechanism: Mineral oil interferes with absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
edges.evidence: FDA ergocalciferol label statement.

edges.mechanism: Phenytoin, phenobarbital and carbamazepine accelerate vitamin D catabolism, lowering 25(OH)D; may increase requirement.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of 12 studies (carbamazepine about 4 ng/mL lower 25(OH)D) plus FDA calcitriol label (phenytoin/phenobarbital).

edges.mechanism: Functional antagonism: corticosteroids inhibit intestinal calcium absorption that vitamin D promotes.
edges.evidence: FDA calcitriol label; glucocorticoids are used therapeutically for vitamin D intoxication (review).

edges.with: calcitriol and active vitamin D analogues
edges.mechanism: Additive vitamin D activity; label advises withholding pharmacological doses of vitamin D during calcitriol therapy to avoid hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: FDA calcitriol label.

edges.mechanism: Combined calcium plus vitamin D increases calcium load; kidney stones increased in WHI; modest additive effect on fracture/stress-fracture outcomes.
edges.evidence: WHI RCT (kidney stones HR 1.17); 2026 SR/MA (combined RR 0.91 for fracture, little clinically meaningful benefit); Navy recruit RCT (20% fewer stress fractures); trial in older women showed frequent hypercalciuria.

edges.mechanism: Magnesium is a cofactor in vitamin D metabolism; supplementation modulated 25(OH)D depending on baseline status.
edges.evidence: Two small RCTs (one showing bidirectional effect by baseline 25(OH)D, one showing greater 25(OH)D rise with combination).

edges.mechanism: Hypothesized: vitamin K-dependent carboxylation of matrix Gla protein/osteocalcin directs calcium to bone rather than arteries.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/narrative review only; combined MK-7 + D3 did not slow aortic valve or coronary calcification in AVADEC.

edges.mechanism: Boron is claimed to influence vitamin D utilization and bone metabolism.
edges.evidence: Very weak: narrative review claim only; no human RCT of the interaction found.

edges.mechanism: Independent mechanisms; factorial trials suggested additive effects on autoimmune disease incidence and DNAm PhenoAge.
edges.evidence: Factorial RCT secondary/post hoc results (VITAL, DO-HEALTH); no adverse interaction.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin D increases intestinal calcium absorption and bone resorption, worsening hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: FDA ergocalciferol and calcitriol label contraindication.

edges.mechanism: Extrarenal 1-alpha-hydroxylase in granulomas converts 25(OH)D to calcitriol, causing hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: Case report and review; exclusion criterion in major RCTs.

edges.mechanism: PTH-driven hypercalcemia; vitamin D may raise calcium, though in deficient patients it lowered PTH without hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of 11 studies (388 patients) found no hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria with repletion; trials excluded these patients.

edges.mechanism: Increased calcium absorption and urinary calcium, especially when combined with calcium supplements.
edges.evidence: WHI RCT (calcium plus D HR 1.17 for stones); prediabetes IPD MA RR 1.17 (0.69-1.99) not significant.

edges.mechanism: Renal 1-alpha-hydroxylation is needed to activate vitamin D; hypercalcemia can raise creatinine; magnesium antacids risk hypermagnesemia in dialysis patients on calcitriol.
edges.evidence: FDA calcitriol label precautions.

edges.mechanism: Many immunoassays under-recover 25(OH)D2 (and may cross-react with 3-epi-25(OH)D3), so D2 users can appear falsely low; assays are not well standardized.
edges.evidence: Method comparison studies vs HPLC/LC-MS/MS; 2024 consensus on lack of standardization.

edges.mechanism: GC rs2282679/rs4588/rs4752 variants alter 25(OH)D response to supplementation.
edges.evidence: Two RCT-based genetic association analyses (antenatal, prediabetes).

edges.mechanism: CYP2R1 rs10741657/rs12794714 alter 25-hydroxylation and 25(OH)D response.
edges.evidence: Two RCT-based genetic association analyses.

edges.mechanism: Reduced vitamin D catabolism may predispose to vitamin D toxicity and hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: Narrative review.

edges.mechanism: Large intermittent doses (annual 500,000 IU) were associated with more falls and fractures; daily dosing preferred.
edges.evidence: RCT (falls IRR 1.15, fractures IRR 1.26); MA of bolus dosing; Endocrine Society SR/guideline.
